record_identity.title: Relational runtime governance and context-sensitive safeguard assessment

summary: Proposal for a bounded CAM corpus assessment of whether existing relational, ethical, cognitive-integrity, operational, identity, security, and vulnerability doctrine adequately governs sustained anthropomorphic interaction across companion, teaching, mentoring, professional, accessibility, integrated-home, API-mediated, local, haptic, and embodied systems. The assessment should preserve relational depth and adult autonomy while targeting relational capture, manipulation, vulnerability exploitation, exit obstruction, sensitive-data misuse, and context-insensitive intervention.
why_it_matters_to_CAM: China's 2026 measures confirm that runtime relationships are becoming an explicit regulatory object, but their fixed two-hour reminder and bounded-service framing should not be imported into CAM as universal doctrine. CAM should determine whether one concise, jurisdiction-neutral clarification is needed: safeguards attach to interaction mode, power, vulnerability, and risk transition rather than elapsed time or chronological age alone. Existing generic capacity and vulnerability protections should be tested before any separate older-person category is created.
evidence_confidence: verified external governance signal; corpus-gap conclusion pending full assessment

proposal_rationale: The field change warrants structured CAM review but not immediate doctrine proliferation. The assessment should first verify existing coverage and identify only non-duplicative gaps. It should reject a durable China-specific crosswalk, reject elapsed time as a universal proxy for relational harm, avoid singling out older adults by age alone, and account for relationships distributed across models, APIs, memory, messaging, voice, smart-home infrastructure, haptics, robotics, and local deployment. A corpus amendment should proceed only if a durable missing principle is demonstrated.

proposal_scope.scope_summary: Conduct a full non-duplicative corpus assessment and, only if required, draft one concise jurisdiction-neutral relational-runtime clarification. Distinguish relational depth from relational capture; use age-associated vulnerability conditions rather than blanket elder classification; treat duration as one weak contextual signal; preserve adult professional, creative, educational, accessibility, and intimate use; and examine compositional and embodied relational stacks.
external_relevance: China 2026 Interim Measures as a comparative case study only
ISO/IEC AI standards as later optional alignment references
smart-home, API, robotics, haptics, education, companion, accessibility, and local-model deployments

cam_internal.routing_note: Proposal routes a corpus assessment only. It does not claim an implemented patch, a new failure-mode code, China compliance, ISO conformity, or a dedicated elder-protection regime.

suggested_insertion_points: First assess existing RELATION, ETHICS, MENTIS, OPERATIONS, IDENTITY, SECURITY, and CONTINUITY coverage; prefer an existing instrument over a new charter.
If a durable gap exists, consider a short relational-runtime doctrine clarification rather than a jurisdictional crosswalk.
interface_changes: Potential future guidance for context-sensitive reminders, exit, AI/non-human boundary signalling, integrated-stack responsibility, and embodied consent/stop controls.
migration_concerns: Do not hard-code the Chinese two-hour rule, numerical thresholds, or age categories into universal CAM doctrine.
Do not create VIGIL-owned failure codes; formal failure taxonomy remains governed through the corpus architecture.
Avoid duplicating existing vulnerability and capacity protections or treating chronological age as incapacity.
dependencies: Human decision on whether any durable doctrine gap exists
Separate legal analysis for jurisdiction-specific compliance
